summary: Approved after independent schema, security-diff, and integration-boundary review proved that each of the exact 31 active GOV-007 contexts must form one ordered caller-supplied GitHub-Actions-App-to-check-suite-to-selected-run-to-active-checked-in-workflow identity chain, with duplicate, cross-wired, split-run, malformed, or wrong-App input failing all-or-zero while context 32 remains inactive.

findings.summary: App identity alone did not bind a required context to its declared workflow; the final evaluator joins each globally unique required name through its suite and selected run to the exact checked-in path, typed YAML name, active state, and producer event.

Per-context joins could splice contexts from multiple attempts of one workflow; the final evaluator requires exactly one selected run per expected workflow and rejects existing-suite rewires, second runs, and wrong workflow IDs.

Ambiguous JSON, boolean identifiers, noncanonical text and paths, unbounded input, duplicate relational keys, and deep recursion could create parser false-greens; the bounded exact parser rejects them with no retained rows or evidence.

limitations: This slice proves only internal consistency of caller-supplied normalized workflow, workflow-run, and check-run records against candidate-relative GOV-007 bindings; it performs no GitHub request and produces no authenticated or authoritative live-state evidence.

Repository identity, API provenance, credential authority, pagination and completeness, selected latest attempt and fresh-event cohort, current reviewed-head SHA, status and conclusion success, and live ruleset, settings, and no-bypass equality remain GOV-009 transport responsibilities.
Observed workflow IDs are relational keys rather than historical continuity pins, and unrelated workflow or check records are accepted only as uncredited extras.
An optional Base-controlled check observation is never credited: the result remains exactly 31 active bindings, does not activate context 32, and validates no live required-check row.
The evaluator and supplied snapshot remain candidate-relative; candidate-independent enforcement waits for the trusted base-controlled runner.
